source_record.bounded_interface_domain: The exact shared item, configuration, time horizon, population and actually used receiving premise in the member are identified. source_record.domain_horizon_authority: Each exact object in the member, with actual horizon and decision rights established rather than presumed from the lineage label.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Conditional analytical receiving consequence; no whole-predicate entailment, empirical net benefit, universal option method, current legal determination or new historical descent.
source_record.native_common_basis: Decision-relevant feasible alternatives are retained only while learning and avoided reversal justify their cost and respect the real convergence deadline.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Parallel exploration, prototypes, scarce skill, delay and loss of an expiring option count. A familiar reversible decision can choose one design with a fallback note.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: An option list treated as joint feasibility.
A confirming experiment rejected because the action remains unchanged.
A prototype treated as complete product qualification.
A partial input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Sunk expenditure treated as future benefit.
Private cost preference treated as authority to waive a binding obligation.

positive_controls.argument: An explicit set of still-feasible options and discriminating elimination criteria make the unresolved choice and planned learning concrete rather than silently treating one design as a settled requirement.
Maintaining options until their relevant constraints are tested can expose an infeasible early point choice before tooling, interfaces or supplier commitments harden.
The candidate set and explicit elimination question identify what a prototype must discriminate and prevent a polished demonstration from standing in for risk-relevant learning.
The actual option set, elimination evidence and convergence costs inform go, hold, redirect or stop and expose a review that occurs after alternatives have already vanished.
Feasible alternative designs and their learning dependencies reveal whether an increment genuinely leaves a costly downstream choice open.
The actual uncertainty, coupling, reversal cost and parallel-learning burden supply context for choosing proportionate evidence and review around convergence.
Parallel effort, convergence deadlines, option value and potential reversal cost identify scenario assumptions omitted by a single-point forecast of the preferred design.
Identified coupling and option loss supply commitment dimensions for the assurance decision, while cheap reversible choices retain a lightweight path.

P2.receiving_bearer: Selection of assurance activities for a context
P2.source_native_proposition: Preserve only decision-relevant alternatives until evidence changes expected regret; record eliminated options and convergence rationale.
P2.receiving_criterion: The chosen controls satisfy binding obligations and address consequential risks with justified omissions, alternatives and retirement conditions.
P2.literal_bridge: The actual uncertainty, coupling, reversal cost and parallel-learning burden supply context for choosing proportionate evidence and review around convergence.

subcondition_evidence.P3: The actual uncertainty, coupling, reversal cost and parallel-learning burden supply context for choosing proportionate evidence and review around convergence.
subcondition_evidence.P4: Applicable obligations, real tailoring authority and the adequacy of the whole control package remain necessary. Control: Keeping several options is not permission to omit binding evidence, and cheap reversible work need not receive a set-based process.

member_to_premise_evidence.reentry: Reopen causally affected members if the design space, constraint, model correspondence, relevant evidence, cost, deadline, authority, obligation or commitment changes. A failed common premise requires all affected members and compositions to be reconsidered; no automatic reverse or transitive inference.
